newsitem.title: CHINA: China bank sets up committee for risk control.
newsitem.headline: China bank sets up committee for risk control.

text.p: The Agricultural Bank of China has set up an auditing and supervising committee to try to to improve internal risk control, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
The committee is the first of its kind set up by a state-owned Chinese bank, Xinhua said. The bank already as a committee to oversee asset-to-liability management and credit extension.
China's commercial banks have been weak in standardising their operations, exercising self-restraint and conducting internal management, Xinhua said.

The new auditing and supervision committee will carry out research and formulate principles and policies for business operation and risk prevention, draw annual objectives and medium and long-term plans for risk examination and evaluation, Xinhua said.
They will make decisions on economic punishment against those accountable for major economic cases and rule violations and propose for criminal punishment when necessary.
China's state-owned banks are burdened with large amounts of bad debt as a result of government policy requiring credit to many state firms.
